content: The test image shows corn plants with prominent reddish-purple/red-brown leaf discoloration on some leaves, with other leaves appearing mostly green. There appears to be some browning/dieback at the top of certain plants. Let me compare with a reference.

**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Corn field with mixed green/reddish-purple leaf coloration
- One prominent leaf showing intense reddish-brown/red-purple discoloration
- Brown dead tissue visible at tops of some plants (top dieback)
- Some overall yellowing on leaves
- No clearly visible discrete small lesion spots (wide-angle field view)

**Comparison with reference:**
The Anthracnose_leaf_spot_top_dieback reference shows oval/spindle-shaped lesions with tan centers and dark brown/purple margins, plus yellow haloing. The test image shows a more diffuse reddish-brown/purple discoloration across a whole leaf and top dieback symptoms.

Key matching features to Anthracnose_leaf_spot_top_dieback:
- Reddish-brown to purple leaf tissue discoloration (severely infected leaves that have progressed)
- Top dieback visible on background plants (brown dead tissue above ears)
- Field-level presentation with lower leaves affected progressing upward

The top dieback (brown dead tissue at plant tops) combined with reddish-purple leaf coloration is characteristic of Anthracnose, where stalk infection above the ear causes the top to die 4-6 weeks after pollination. The class "Anthracnose_leaf_spot_top_dieback" covers both the leaf spot and top dieback presentations.
